podcast.body: This song, from "The Downward Spiral" (1994), was among those accused by Mark Anofrio of being plagiarized from his "Elephant Man" compositions. "He says, closer, hurt, march of the pigs, Mr. Self-destruct, and downward spiral are all ripoffs of Elephant Man."

podcast.body: A lullaby rendition of this Nine Inch Nails song is featured on the "Rockabye Baby" series of CDs, which adapt rock songs for infants.

podcast.title: Innovative Sampling and Digital Effects
podcast.body: The opening sounds of Nine Inch Nails' hit song "Closer," from the album *The Downward Spiral*, were created using advanced digital recording and sampling techniques. Trent Reznor sampled the opening of Iggy Pop's 1977 song "Nightclubbing" from *The Idiot*, recorded it into a Mac running Pro Tools, inverted the waveform, and applied various digital effects. He also added samples from a Roland TR-808 drum machine and processed everything through a Roland R70 machine, resulting in entirely new sounds. "Trent recorded that bit from the Iggy Pop album into his Mac, which was running an early version of Pro Tools."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
